speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some skin concerns to discuss; to properly evaluate any potential oncologic implications, where exactly are these lesions located and how would you describe their appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the history of smoking and failed treatments for syphilis are important. Can you describe the specific texture, color, and size of the lesions on your penis and finger, and have you noticed any bleeding or pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, CBC. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: The latest measurement readings are normal, which is good news for your systemic status. However, the history of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on your penis and finger, combined with your heavy smoking history, raises concern for squamous cell carcinoma. Can you tell me if the lesion on your penis has been growing, and do you have any visible bleeding or pain? REQUEST IMAGES: Penile_Lesion, Finger_Lesion.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lesions are described as painless, crusty, red, and non-healing on both the penile shaft and your left middle finger. Given your significant smoking history and the failure of previous treatments for syphilis and eczema, we are highly concerned for Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Have you noticed any ulceration or induration (hardening) of these areas, and do you have any history of HPV infection or genital warts in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Digits). The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions on the penile shaft and finger in a heavy smoker with a history of failed syphilis treatment is highly characteristic of this malignancy. Immediate biopsy is indicated to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
